territorial_scope.description: Applies to intermediaries subject to the legislative authority of Parliament that make Canadian news content available to persons in Canada; eligible news businesses are designated by Commission order.

evidence.quote: that is subject to the legislative authority of Parliament and that makes news content produced by news outlets available to persons in Canada

summary.short: Regulates digital news intermediaries (search engines, social media) with significant bargaining power over news businesses. Requires operator notification, bargaining with eligible news businesses over compensation for news content with final-offer arbitration, anti-discrimination rules, and Commission oversight. Initial provisions in force 19 December 2023.
summary.long: The Online News Act applies to digital news intermediaries (online communications platforms, including search engines and social media services, that make news content produced by news outlets available to persons in Canada) where the operator has a significant bargaining power imbalance with news businesses, assessed by size, strategic market advantage and prominent market position (s. 6). Operators must notify the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission (s. 7). Eligible news businesses may start bargaining over compensation for news content: 90 days of negotiation, 120 days of mediation, then final offer arbitration for 45 days limited to monetary disputes (s. 19). Operators may request exemption orders based on agreements meeting listed criteria, and the Commission may issue interim orders (ss. 11-12). Operators must bargain in good faith and must not unjustly discriminate against or give undue preference to eligible businesses, including themselves (ss. 22, 51). A code of conduct is to be made by regulation (s. 49). Sections 45 and 90.1 of the Competition Act do not apply to covered activities (ss. 47-48). Enforcement includes Commission compliance and conditions orders, administrative monetary penalties of up to $25,000 for an individual and $10 million for an entity on a first violation, and civil recovery of agreement payments (ss. 45-46, 50, 59-61). Certain provisions were in force 19 December 2023; others by order in council or 180 days after royal assent (s. 93). The Minister must cause a review before the fifth anniversary of the day section 87 comes into force (s. 87).

digital news intermediary means an online communications platform, including a search engine or social media service, that is subject to the legislative authority of Parliament
operator means an individual or entity that, through any means, operates a digital news intermediary.
news business means an individual or entity that operates a news outlet in Canada.

news outlet means an undertaking or any distinct part of an undertaking whose primary purpose is to produce news content and includes an Indigenous news outlet or an official language minority community news outlet.
news content means content — in any format, including an audio or audiovisual format — that reports on, investigates or explains current issues or events of public interest
news content is made available if
eligible in relation to a news business, means that the business is designated under subsection 27(1).
an agreement that is entered into as a result of bargaining sessions referred to in paragraph 19(1)(a) or mediation sessions referred to in paragraph 19(1)(b)
Indigenous news outlet means an undertaking or any distinct part of an undertaking whose primary purpose is to produce news content

definitions.term: official language minority community news outlet

evidence.quote: official language minority community news outlet means an undertaking or any distinct part of an undertaking whose primary purpose is to produce news content and that produces news content primarily for an official language minority community.
official language minority community means English-speaking communities in Quebec and French-speaking communities outside Quebec.
entity includes a corporation or a trust, partnership, fund, joint venture or any other unincorporated association or organization.
Indigenous peoples has the meaning assigned by the definition aboriginal peoples of Canada in subsection 35(2) of the Constitution Act, 1982.

enforcement.triggered_by: Failure by an operator, eligible news business or group of eligible news businesses to comply with the code of conduct
enforcement.max_penalty_text: No monetary maximum stated; order requires any measure the Commission considers necessary to remedy the non-compliance

evidence.quote: the Commission may, by order, require the operator, business or group to take any measure the Commission considers necessary to remedy the non-compliance

enforcement.authority: Court of competent jurisdiction (application by a party to the covered agreement)
enforcement.triggered_by: Non-compliance with a provision of a covered agreement
enforcement.max_penalty_text: No monetary maximum stated; court order directing compliance with the provision

evidence.quote: a party to the agreement may, in addition to any other remedy available, apply to a court of competent jurisdiction for an order directing compliance with the provision

enforcement.authority: Court of competent jurisdiction (civil recovery by eligible news business or group)
enforcement.triggered_by: Non-payment of payments due under a covered agreement during the period specified in the agreement
enforcement.max_penalty_text: No penalty; recovery of payments due

evidence.quote: collect payments due under it and, if they are not made, recover the payments in a court of competent jurisdiction
